blocks.content: Image size is not just an aesthetic concern, it is a direct performance and cost factor: every pull, every deploy, every scale-out event moves that many bytes across the network, every single time.
1. Size Directly Determines Pull and Deploy Speed
blocks.text: 1. Size Directly Determines Pull and Deploy Speed

blocks.content: A 1.2GB image takes meaningfully longer to pull than an 80MB one, on every single machine that needs it, that difference shows up directly as slower deploys and slower autoscaling, exactly when speed usually matters most.

blocks.alt: Every byte in the image is a byte that has to move, every time

blocks.content: A slow pull on one machine is an inconvenience, the same slow pull repeated across a hundred nodes during a deploy or an autoscale event is a genuine bottleneck, the size cost is paid independently by every single node that needs the image.

blocks.alt: The same size cost, paid again by every node that pulls it

blocks.content: 3. A Real Line Item, Not Just a Speed Concern
blocks.text: 3. A Real Line Item, Not Just a Speed Concern

blocks.content: Beyond speed, image size has a direct cost dimension too, registry storage scales with image size and version history, and bandwidth is a real, metered cost on most cloud platforms, larger images are, quite literally, more expensive to store and move.

blocks.alt: Storage and bandwidth costs scale directly with image size

blocks.content: 4. The Techniques Themselves Are Covered Elsewhere
blocks.text: 4. The Techniques Themselves Are Covered Elsewhere

blocks.content: The actual how-to for shrinking an image, small base images, multi-stage builds, combining and cleaning up layers, is covered in full in the Docker Build module's Image Optimization topic. This topic is specifically about why that effort pays off in real performance and cost terms, not a repeat of the mechanics.

blocks.alt: The techniques live in Docker Build, this topic covers why they matter

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: Image size is a direct performance lever, pull time, deploy speed, and autoscale responsiveness all scale with it, on every node that pulls the image.
Beyond speed, size is a real, ongoing cost, registry storage and bandwidth both scale with it, not just a one-time deploy delay.
